summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a male with multiple myeloma on carfilzomib, chronic diastolic heart failure, diabetes with neuropathy and nephropathy, and a history of hemolytic anemia, was admitted for left lower extremity cellulitis. He presented with three days of increasing redness, warmth, and swelling without fever. He was started on IV vancomycin and Zosyn, with improvement in symptoms and inflammatory markers. Blood cultures were negative, DVT ultrasound was negative, and Lyme serology was non-reactive. He was transitioned to oral cephalexin for a 10-day course. His hemoglobin remained stable, and his kidney function improved to baseline. He was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up planned in oncology and primary care.
